content.thinking:
Test Flight is one-shot — it boots a server, runs RCON checks, then stops, so there's no persistent live console for reload. For the config flight, I can combine writing config.yml with a reload command within that single flight, since the RCON check step lets me run `writeFile` followed by `<cmd> reload`. But to wire deliverConfig through the orchestrator for real use, I'd need a genuinely live server session rather than this one-shot flight.

For the mob-stat flight specifically, I'm planning to build a fixture mod jar using a generated config accessor, compile it, and then verify behavior: boot with default config, spawn a zombie, check its default attributes via RCON, then apply a new config through my pure-core writer (preserving comments), deliver it with writeFile + reload, and confirm the mob's stats update — using vanilla attribute/data commands like `attribute @e[...] minecraft:max_health base get` as an independent verification path.

I'm also thinking through how to test invalid/out-of-range values: the studio validation should reject them at the pure/record layer, while a hand-edited bad config.yml dropped directly onto the server should trigger the plugin's generated accessor to clamp to hard limits and log "clamped". I'm weighing whether to run the deliverConfig orchestrator against a local filesystem host to simulate the full "edit in studio → deliver → reload" flow, concluding the cleanest approach is: boot with the old config, then have RCON write the newly delivered config and issue a reload command to simulate a genuine live update rather than a fresh boot.

Now I'm sketching out the module layout for the config library — a spec.ts for the Zod-based ConfigSpec schema and structural validation, templates.ts for the twelve category templates and instantiation helpers, values.ts for value validation/clamping/coercion plus preset handling, and diff.ts for computing and applying patches between config revisions.

For yaml.ts, I need comment-preserving YAML parsing and writing tailored to typical Bukkit config.yml files: nested maps, scalars, inline and block lists, and both full-line and trailing comments. I should check whether the `yaml` package in node_modules supports comment preservation, since rolling my own would be a lot more work.

# Cyrus Config and Stats Studio: design + plan (v5, 2026-10-10)

Owner request: every number a mod can tune (mob health and speed, weapon fire rate, ability cooldowns, shop prices, boss phases, quest rewards, arena timers...) gets a manual editor. Nobody has to prompt the AI to change a number. Cyrus knows which tunables to OFFER for each kind of mod. Stats with a visual (walk speed, attack speed, scale) play live in the viewport. Game-neutral schema; per-game exporters apply it. Branch `feature/cyrus-r23-config`, code in `lib/cyrus/config/`.

## 1. ConfigSpec v1 (the one param model)

```
ConfigSpec { schemaVersion: 1, file: "config.yml", category?, reload?: { command }, groups[], params[], presets[] }
Group      { id, label, help?, order? }
Param      { key (dotted config path), group, type, label (<=60), help? (one line, <=200), default,
             unit?, min?, max?, step?, safe?: { min?, max?, note? }, options? (enum), item? (list), columns? (table),
             maxLength? (text), assetKind? (asset-ref), applies: "live" | "reload" | "restart",
             visual?: { channel, clip?, ref }, tags[], advanced?, readOnly? }
Preset     { id ("easy" | "normal" | "hard" | own id), label, values: { key: value } }
```

Types: `number` (float), `int`, `range` ([lo, hi], e.g. spawn group size), `bool`, `enum` (options with labels), `text` (maxLength, single line), `color` (#rrggbb), `duration` (a number with a storage unit `ticks|s|ms`; the editor shows seconds), `sound-ref` (namespaced key, Sound Library id), `asset-ref` (texture/model/sound id of this project), `list` (scalars of one item type, maxItems), `table` (rows of typed columns: drop tables, shop price lists, wave lists, maxRows).

Two kinds of limits: `min/max` are HARD limits (the generated loader clamps to them, the editor refuses values outside them); `safe` is the BALANCE range (outside it the editor shows a warning, "Zombies at 500 health take ~80 hits with a diamond sword", but saves). Hard limits always contain the safe range and the default (validator rule).

`applies` says how a change reaches a running server: `live` (the mod re-reads the value without a command, rare), `reload` (`/<plugin> reload`; needs `reload.command`), `restart`. A spec without a reload command cannot declare `reload` (validator turns it into an error). The studio shows the strongest one among the changed keys as a badge and the delivery uses it.

`visual` links a stat to the viewport/motion core: channels `clipRate` (the named clip plays at value/ref speed: moveSpeed 0.35 vs ref 0.23 plays the walk clip 1.52x), `attackRate` (attack clip rate), `scale` (uniform model scale = value/ref), `fireRate` (gun fire clip / muzzle-flash interval), `tint` (color). `visualEffects(spec, values)` is pure and returns `{ clipRates: { walk: 1.52 }, scale: 1.2, ... }`; `applyToClock(clock, effects, clip)` calls `setSpeed` on anything with that method, so it works with Model Studio's `PlaybackClock` (r16) today and the Motion core's `createClock` (r21) when merged. No import of either.

Designer params are the same model: `fromDesignerParams(Param[])` maps the designers' `num/ticks/int/text/sound` params (min/max caps, role, path) into ConfigSpec params (`number/duration(ticks)/int/text/sound-ref`, hard limits = caps, tags = role, applies = reload via `/<cmd> reload`). The designers keep emitting their own config.yml byte-identically; the studio edits their values through ConfigSpec, and a values-only change is written into config.yml with the comment-preserving writer (no Java recompiled). One editor, one value model, one validator.

## 2. Relation to ModSpec

ModSpec v1 gets an optional `config` section: `{ spec: ConfigSpec, values?: { key: value } }` (optional, so every stored spec stays valid; JSON Schema regenerated). The schema is part of the mod (it changes only with a build); the values change in studio revisions. `validateModSpec` checks the section (keys unique, defaults within limits, presets reference real keys).

## 3. Category templates (what Cyrus offers by default)

Templates are data (`lib/cyrus/config/templates.ts`), keyed by template id, mapped from the universal categories. Each lists groups, params with default, unit, hard + safe range, applies, visual, and easy/normal/hard presets.

- **mob/creature**: max health, armor, movement speed (visual clipRate walk), follow range, attack damage, attack speed (attackRate), knockback, knockback resistance, scale (visual scale), XP drop, drops table (item, chance, min, max), spawn weight, group size (range), light level max, spawn biomes (list), despawn, glow color.
- **melee weapon**: attack damage, attack speed (attackRate swing), reach, knockback, crit multiplier, durability, sweep, enchantability, special-hit chance.
- **ranged weapon / gun**: damage, fire rate (rounds/min, visual fireRate), magazine size, reserve ammo, reload time (duration, visual clipRate reload), spread (degrees), recoil, projectile speed, range, falloff start, headshot multiplier, fire mode (enum semi/burst/auto), burst count, ammo item (asset-ref), fire sound (sound-ref).
- **armor**: armor points, toughness, knockback resistance, durability, set bonus effect + level, movement penalty.
- **ability/spell**: cooldown, range, strength, damage, heal, duration, mana/charge cost, charges, cast time, area radius, sound.
- **boss/encounter**: health, phase thresholds (list of %), damage per phase (table), enrage time, minion count, arena radius, bossbar color/text, loot table, respawn time.
- **shop/economy**: currency name, starting balance, price table (item, buy, sell, stock), sell multiplier, tax %, daily limit, interest.
- **quest/NPC**: objective counts, reward money, reward XP, reward items table, cooldown/repeat, time limit, NPC name, dialogue text lines.
- **minigame/arena**: min/max players, countdown, round time, rounds, lives, respawn delay, team count, kill score, win score, border size, kit list.
- **world/dimension**: ore vein size, veins per chunk, height range (range), structure spacing/separation, mob cap, day length, weather chance (restart applies).
- **custom item**: name, lore lines, rarity color, stack size, cooldown, uses/durability, effect + level + duration.
- **utility/admin plugin**: messages (text), prefix, colors, feature toggles (bool), intervals, permission defaults, limits, log level.

`templateIdsForCategory("creatures") -> ["mob"]` and `suggestTemplates(prompt)` (keyword table, zero tokens) choose them. Mods can declare params outside templates; templates are what Cyrus offers, not a cage.

## 4. How the AI declares tunables, and how the build verifies them

Prompt (new section, only when the build has `config` on): "Declare every tunable in `assets/config/schema.json` (ConfigSpec). Start from the template keys for this category (given in the request); add your own; read each key in code through `getConfig()` with the exact key string; never hard-code a number that has a key." The template's key list for the routed category goes in the user turn (system prompt stays cacheable).

Build checks (pure, in `lib/cyrus/config/verify.ts`, bundled into the service like designer-spec.js):
1. schema validates (Zod + rules).
2. every declared key is READ by the Java sources: the exact key string appears in a `getConfig()/getX("key")` style call or in the generated accessor's use. Unread key = error (a setting that does nothing is worse than none).
3. keys read in code but not declared = warning (listed so the editor still shows them via inference).
4. cheap magic-number heuristic: numeric literals passed to known stat APIs (`setBaseValue`, `setDamage`, `setCooldown`, `runTaskTimer` periods, `setVelocity(...multiply(n))`, `setFireTicks`) = warning with file and line, not a block.
5. config.yml is GENERATED from the schema (`renderConfigYml`): header, each group as a comment block, one `# label (unit, min-max). help` comment per key, defaults. If the model wrote its own config.yml it is merged: its comments and unknown keys are kept, declared keys added where missing.

Designer builds are unchanged (they already make every number a setting); their schema is derived from `designParams`.

## 5. Storage (values only)

A studio save is a new `CyrusRevision` kind `config` (pure kind list extended; the column is a string, no migration) whose manifest is the head's with config.yml's new sha, plus a `CyrusProjectAsset` row kind `config`, key `values`, provenance `{ values, specSha256, configYml, patch }`. No model call, no build, no token charge. The head check (expectedHeadId) gives 409 on a stale editor. Undo = a new revision with the previous values (revert never edits history).

## 6. Delivery

`deliverConfig(serverId, { projectId, revisionId, pluginName, configYml, applies, reloadCommand }, host)` runs through the orchestrator's existing transaction (journal, recover check, rollback): write `plugins/<plugin>/config.yml` through the journal, then apply as declared: `reload` -> the plugin's reload command over the console (a failure reply rolls back and re-runs reload on the old file), `restart` -> restart + health, `live` -> nothing. Health: plugin still enabled, no new error lines. Behind the existing `CYRUS_DELIVERY` and the new `CYRUS_CONFIG_STUDIO` (both off).

## 7. Imported mods: schema inference

`inferSchema(configYml, { pluginYml? })`: every scalar leaf becomes a param. Type from value (bool, int, number, `#hex` color, namespaced `sound` key, list); `duration` from `_ticks/_seconds/_ms` suffixes; unit from key words (health hp, speed, damage, radius/range blocks, chance/percent %, price/cost/money currency); label from the key; help from the comment above or on the line; hard limits from comments (`(0-100)`, `between 1 and 5`, `min: 1`, `max 20`), enum options from `one of: a, b, c` / `a|b|c`; groups from top-level sections; `applies` = reload when plugin.yml declares a command with a reload usage, else restart. Inferred specs are marked `inferred: true`, never get balance warnings they cannot justify, and keep every unknown key untouched on write.

## 8. Presets, diff, reset, undo

Presets per template (easy/normal/hard) + "custom" (whatever differs). `applyPreset` only touches keys the preset names. `diffValues(a, b)` lists `{ key, from, to }`; `applyPatch`, `invertPatch` (undo), `resetKeys(keys)` (back to defaults), `resetAll`. The editor shows changed keys, the diff before save, and which keys need reload/restart.

## 9. Per-game exporter contract

```
ConfigExporter { game, formats: ["yaml" | "json" | "toml" | "cfg"], applies: (live|reload|restart)[], reloadVerified: bool,
  render(spec, values, previousText?) -> { path, text }, read(text, spec) -> values, maturity }
```
Minecraft Paper: YAML at `plugins/<plugin>/config.yml`, reload by plugin command (verified on 1.21.11 + 26.2 here). Datapack-only mods: values become generated data files (restart/`minecraft:reload`), later. Other games: planned (FiveM `config.lua`, Hytale JSON) with maturity "planned".

## 10. Studio UI

`/dashboard/cyrus/<id>/studio/config`: groups in a left rail, search, a form generated from the schema (sliders + number inputs with units for bounded numbers, toggles, selects, color, duration in seconds, sound picker by key, list chips, table rows), preset chips, per-field reset, balance warnings inline, `applies` badges, a diff drawer with Save (revision) and Deliver. A preview panel (creature/weapon) with a clock that follows visual stats. Dark + light, narrow read-only.

## 11. "Just tweak a setting" recogniser

`planConfigEdit(text, spec)` mirrors the designers' `planDesignEdit` grammar (set X to N [unit]) against labels, keys and tags. Wire only if every clause resolves to exactly one key and the value is within hard limits; anything else goes to the model. Proposed: wire behind `CYRUS_CONFIG_STUDIO`, owner decides whether skipping the model is free.

## 12. Risks

- The model declares keys it never reads, or reads keys with a typo: verify step 2/3 catches both; magic numbers are only heuristic.
- A reload command that does not re-read everything (plain AI plugins): `applies` comes from the model; a real flight per build is the only proof. Default to `restart` when unsure.
- YAML subset: anchors, multi-document files and block scalars are kept byte-identical but not editable.
- Balance numbers in templates are judgement, not measurement.
- Imported mods: inferred ranges may be wrong; inferred params never clamp, they only validate type.

## 13. Owner decisions

1. Plan gate: editing numbers is not asset creation. Proposed UNGATED on every plan (server-side ownership/auth only, fail closed).
2. Values-only saves and deliveries cost 0 tokens?
3. Wire the "just tweak a setting" recogniser (skips the model)?
4. Automatic reload after delivery, or a "Deliver" click per change?
5. Show balance warnings to customers, or only to the owner/admin first?
6. Flag `CYRUS_CONFIG_STUDIO` order: after `CYRUS_DELIVERY`.

Two kinds of limits: `min/max` are HARD limits (the generated loader clamps to them, the editor refuses values outside them); `safe` is the BALANCE range (outside it the editor shows a warning, "Zombies at 500 health take ~80 hits with a diamond sword", but saves). Hard limits always contain the safe range and the default (validator rule).

`applies` says how a change reaches a running server: `live` (the mod re-reads the value without a command, rare), `reload` (`/<plugin> reload`; needs `reload.command`), `restart`. A spec without a reload command cannot declare `reload` (validator turns it into an error). The studio shows the strongest one among the changed keys as a badge and the delivery uses it.

`visual` links a stat to the viewport/motion core: channels `clipRate` (the named clip plays at value/ref speed: moveSpeed 0.35 vs ref 0.23 plays the walk clip 1.52x), `attackRate` (attack clip rate), `scale` (uniform model scale = value/ref), `fireRate` (gun fire clip / muzzle-flash interval), `tint` (color). `visualEffects(spec, values)` is pure and returns `{ clipRates: { walk: 1.52 }, scale: 1.2, ... }`; `applyToClock(clock, effects, clip)` calls `setSpeed` on anything with that method, so it works with Model Studio's `PlaybackClock` (r16) today and the Motion core's `createClock` (r21) when merged. No import of either.

Designer params are the same model: `fromDesignerParams(Param[])` maps the designers' `num/ticks/int/text/sound` params (min/max caps, role, path) into ConfigSpec params (`number/duration(ticks)/int/text/sound-ref`, hard limits = caps, tags = role, applies = reload via `/<cmd> reload`). The designers keep emitting their own config.yml byte-identically; the studio edits their values through ConfigSpec, and a values-only change is written into config.yml with the comment-preserving writer (no Java recompiled). One editor, one value model, one validator.

## 2. Relation to ModSpec

ModSpec v1 gets an optional `config` section: `{ spec: ConfigSpec, values?: { key: value } }` (optional, so every stored spec stays valid; JSON Schema regenerated). The schema is part of the mod (it changes only with a build); the values change in studio revisions. `validateModSpec` checks the section (keys unique, defaults within limits, presets reference real keys).

## 3. Category templates (what Cyrus offers by default)

Templates are data (`lib/cyrus/config/templates.ts`), keyed by template id, mapped from the universal categories. Each lists groups, params with default, unit, hard + safe range, applies, visual, and easy/normal/hard presets.

- **mob/creature**: max health, armor, movement speed (visual clipRate walk), follow range, attack damage, attack speed (attackRate), knockback, knockback resistance, scale (visual scale), XP drop, drops table (item, chance, min, max), spawn weight, group size (range), light level max, spawn biomes (list), despawn, glow color.
- **melee weapon**: attack damage, attack speed (attackRate swing), reach, knockback, crit multiplier, durability, sweep, enchantability, special-hit chance.
- **ranged weapon / gun**: damage, fire rate (rounds/min, visual fireRate), magazine size, reserve ammo, reload time (duration, visual clipRate reload), spread (degrees), recoil, projectile speed, range, falloff start, headshot multiplier, fire mode (enum semi/burst/auto), burst count, ammo item (asset-ref), fire sound (sound-ref).
- **armor**: armor points, toughness, knockback resistance, durability, set bonus effect + level, movement penalty.
- **ability/spell**: cooldown, range, strength, damage, heal, duration, mana/charge cost, charges, cast time, area radius, sound.
- **boss/encounter**: health, phase thresholds (list of %), damage per phase (table), enrage time, minion count, arena radius, bossbar color/text, loot table, respawn time.
- **shop/economy**: currency name, starting balance, price table (item, buy, sell, stock), sell multiplier, tax %, daily limit, interest.
- **quest/NPC**: objective counts, reward money, reward XP, reward items table, cooldown/repeat, time limit, NPC name, dialogue text lines.
- **minigame/arena**: min/max players, countdown, round time, rounds, lives, respawn delay, team count, kill score, win score, border size, kit list.
- **world/dimension**: ore vein size, veins per chunk, height range (range), structure spacing/separation, mob cap, day length, weather chance (restart applies).
- **custom item**: name, lore lines, rarity color, stack size, cooldown, uses/durability, effect + level + duration.
- **utility/admin plugin**: messages (text), prefix, colors, feature toggles (bool), intervals, permission defaults, limits, log level.

`templateIdsForCategory("creatures") -> ["mob"]` and `suggestTemplates(prompt)` (keyword table, zero tokens) choose them. Mods can declare params outside templates; templates are what Cyrus offers, not a cage.

## 4. How the AI declares tunables, and how the build verifies them

Prompt (new section, only when the build has `config` on): "Declare every tunable in `assets/config/schema.json` (ConfigSpec). Start from the template keys for this category (given in the request); add your own; read each key in code through `getConfig()` with the exact key string; never hard-code a number that has a key." The template's key list for the routed category goes in the user turn (system prompt stays cacheable).

Build checks (pure, in `lib/cyrus/config/verify.ts`, bundled into the service like designer-spec.js):
1. schema validates (Zod + rules).
2. every declared key is READ by the Java sources: the exact key string appears in a `getConfig()/getX("key")` style call or in the generated accessor's use. Unread key = error (a setting that does nothing is worse than none).
3. keys read in code but not declared = warning (listed so the editor still shows them via inference).
4. cheap magic-number heuristic: numeric literals passed to known stat APIs (`setBaseValue`, `setDamage`, `setCooldown`, `runTaskTimer` periods, `setVelocity(...multiply(n))`, `setFireTicks`) = warning with file and line, not a block.
5. config.yml is GENERATED from the schema (`renderConfigYml`): header, each group as a comment block, one `# label (unit, min-max). help` comment per key, defaults. If the model wrote its own config.yml it is merged: its comments and unknown keys are kept, declared keys added where missing.

Designer builds are unchanged (they already make every number a setting); their schema is derived from `designParams`.

## 5. Storage (values only)

A studio save is a new `CyrusRevision` kind `config` (pure kind list extended; the column is a string, no migration) whose manifest is the head's with config.yml's new sha, plus a `CyrusProjectAsset` row kind `config`, key `values`, provenance `{ values, specSha256, configYml, patch }`. No model call, no build, no token charge. The head check (expectedHeadId) gives 409 on a stale editor. Undo = a new revision with the previous values (revert never edits history).

## 6. Delivery

`deliverConfig(serverId, { projectId, revisionId, pluginName, configYml, applies, reloadCommand }, host)` runs through the orchestrator's existing transaction (journal, recover check, rollback): write `plugins/<plugin>/config.yml` through the journal, then apply as declared: `reload` -> the plugin's reload command over the console (a failure reply rolls back and re-runs reload on the old file), `restart` -> restart + health, `live` -> nothing. Health: plugin still enabled, no new error lines. Behind the existing `CYRUS_DELIVERY` and the new `CYRUS_CONFIG_STUDIO` (both off).

## 7. Imported mods: schema inference

`inferSchema(configYml, { pluginYml? })`: every scalar leaf becomes a param. Type from value (bool, int, number, `#hex` color, namespaced `sound` key, list); `duration` from `_ticks/_seconds/_ms` suffixes; unit from key words (health hp, speed, damage, radius/range blocks, chance/percent %, price/cost/money currency); label from the key; help from the comment above or on the line; hard limits from comments (`(0-100)`, `between 1 and 5`, `min: 1`, `max 20`), enum options from `one of: a, b, c` / `a|b|c`; groups from top-level sections; `applies` = reload when plugin.yml declares a command with a reload usage, else restart. Inferred specs are marked `inferred: true`, never get balance warnings they cannot justify, and keep every unknown key untouched on write.

## 8. Presets, diff, reset, undo

Presets per template (easy/normal/hard) + "custom" (whatever differs). `applyPreset` only touches keys the preset names. `diffValues(a, b)` lists `{ key, from, to }`; `applyPatch`, `invertPatch` (undo), `resetKeys(keys)` (back to defaults), `resetAll`. The editor shows changed keys, the diff before save, and which keys need reload/restart.

## 9. Per-game exporter contract

```
ConfigExporter { game, formats: ["yaml" | "json" | "toml" | "cfg"], applies: (live|reload|restart)[], reloadVerified: bool,
  render(spec, values, previousText?) -> { path, text }, read(text, spec) -> values, maturity }
```
Minecraft Paper: YAML at `plugins/<plugin>/config.yml`, reload by plugin command (verified on 1.21.11 + 26.2 here). Datapack-only mods: values become generated data files (restart/`minecraft:reload`), later. Other games: planned (FiveM `config.lua`, Hytale JSON) with maturity "planned".

## 10. Studio UI

`/dashboard/cyrus/<id>/studio/config`: groups in a left rail, search, a form generated from the schema (sliders + number inputs with units for bounded numbers, toggles, selects, color, duration in seconds, sound picker by key, list chips, table rows), preset chips, per-field reset, balance warnings inline, `applies` badges, a diff drawer with Save (revision) and Deliver. A preview panel (creature/weapon) with a clock that follows visual stats. Dark + light, narrow read-only.

## 11. "Just tweak a setting" recogniser

`planConfigEdit(text, spec)` mirrors the designers' `planDesignEdit` grammar (set X to N [unit]) against labels, keys and tags. Wire only if every clause resolves to exactly one key and the value is within hard limits; anything else goes to the model. Proposed: wire behind `CYRUS_CONFIG_STUDIO`, owner decides whether skipping the model is free.

## 12. Risks

- The model declares keys it never reads, or reads keys with a typo: verify step 2/3 catches both; magic numbers are only heuristic.
- A reload command that does not re-read everything (plain AI plugins): `applies` comes from the model; a real flight per build is the only proof. Default to `restart` when unsure.
- YAML subset: anchors, multi-document files and block scalars are kept byte-identical but not editable.
- Balance numbers in templates are judgement, not measurement.
- Imported mods: inferred ranges may be wrong; inferred params never clamp, they only validate type.

## 13. Owner decisions

1. Plan gate: editing numbers is not asset creation. Proposed UNGATED on every plan (server-side ownership/auth only, fail closed).
2. Values-only saves and deliveries cost 0 tokens?
3. Wire the "just tweak a setting" recogniser (skips the model)?
4. Automatic reload after delivery, or a "Deliver" click per change?
5. Show balance warnings to customers, or only to the owner/admin first?
6. Flag `CYRUS_CONFIG_STUDIO` order: after `CYRUS_DELIVERY`.

content.thinking:
Now I'm setting up a real test config for node-2, defining a mob template spec for a frost zombie with a reload command and a restricted set of attributes to include like health, speed, attack damage, knockback resistance, and scale, checking which attributes actually exist in this version.

For the hand-written Java fixture plugin, I'm designing the FrostMobs plugin: it loads settings through a generated CyrusSettings class, and exposes a /frostmobs command with spawn, stats, and reload subcommands that spawn a tagged, persistent, non-despawning zombie, report its live attribute values, and reapply stats after config reloads with a confirmation message.

I also need to handle daylight burning and peaceful-difficulty despawning for the zombie, likely by disabling burn-in-day behavior and setting it to not despawn or be removed when far away, while planning to verify base attribute values independently through vanilla attribute commands against the expected numeric output format across different server versions.

Then for the actual flow per lane: first the build step generates the config yaml, settings class, fixture, and plugin.yml, verifies all tunables are read via accessor, then compiles and jars everything; second, the studio path uses an in-memory store with default config and plugin.yml sources, saving new values for health, speed, damage, and scale before reading the config back.

I also need to test saving an invalid value (health 5000) and confirm it gets rejected with an invalid_values error, then record that outcome. For delivery, I'm using a local filesystem copy with the existing plugin jar and old config to produce a merged config.yml, with a console stub recording the reload command and response — noting that this stub can't reflect a truly live reload, which I should document. Finally I'm sketching the RCON command sequence for the flight check, starting with listing plugins to confirm FrostMobs is present.

Then I'm laying out the rest of the RCON sequence: setting difficulty to easy, spawning a frost zombie and checking its stats match the default values (health 20, speed 0.23, damage 3, scale 1), verifying via the attribute command, then delivering the new config and reloading to confirm it reports "config reloaded" without any clamping. After that I check stats again for the new values (health 60, speed 0.3, damage 7, scale 1.5), confirm via attribute commands, spawn another zombie to verify new mobs get the updated stats, and finally test an out-of-range config (health 5000, invalid speed) to confirm reload clamps the value down to 1024 as expected.

I'm also noting that an invalid (non-numeric) speed value should fall back to the default of 0.23 rather than the previous value, since my parsing uses a fallback default — I'll need to document this behavior. Then I'm planning the test lanes: running on 1.21.11 (JDK21) and 26.2 (JDK25) via devhost with locking since these are heavier runs on node-2, using the local-remote test flight runner.

Now I'm starting the Java fixture plugin, setting up the necessary Paper API imports for attributes, entities, commands, and the plugin class...

Writing plugin class...

Setting up the spawned zombie with the scoreboard tag, persistence, no AI, and no burning, then applying it and replying confirmation; for the stats command I'm iterating over all worlds to count tagged zombies.

For the reload command I'm reloading the config, reapplying settings to existing zombies, and replying with a count of updates. I'm also double-checking that `Attribute.MAX_HEALTH` and `setShouldBurnInDay` are valid API calls for this Paper version.

Rather than risk the burn-in-day method, I'll just make the zombie invulnerable to sidestep sunlight damage entirely while also disabling AI, which should be simpler and safer than fiddling with burn flags. I'm also sorting out number formatting for the stats output so values like health and speed display cleanly.

I need to make sure the zombie persists and that the world's chunk is actually loaded at spawn, and I'm weighing whether difficulty needs adjusting so it doesn't despawn or get removed unexpectedly. The scale attribute should work fine since it's been available since 1.20.5, and I'm double-checking the base movement speed value matches expectations before verifying everything through an attribute query command.

I'm now sketching out the plugin.yml structure—name, main class, api-version matching the server build, the frostmobs command with its usage string and permission node—plus the jar build process using javac and the jar tool to mirror a real build pipeline. I'm also starting to think through the delivery mechanism for the test flight script, using a local temp directory under /opt/mc as the deployment target.

Then I'm weighing how the plugin jar and config get placed into opt/mc/plugins so inventory scanning picks them up, and wrestling with how to make the console/reload step and health check behave realistically without triggering a false rollback from a fake "simulated" health failure.

I'm thinking about ordering constraints: since health evaluation happens before deliverConfig returns, I can't just defer the console command and expect the health check to reflect a subsequent flight. A two-phase approach might work better -- running deliverConfig locally first with a console that queues the command, then handling health separately.

For this to work in a single flight, the server needs to boot with the old config, then the delivered config file gets written, and only then does the queued reload command execute -- meaning deliverConfig has to run before the flight itself starts.

Actually, I think I'm overcomplicating this. Let me simplify: Flight 0 just boots with the default config and verifies plugins are enabled, as a clean baseline before layering in the delivery logic.

Trying a cleaner path: skip Flight 0 entirely and fold the plugin-enabled check into the delivery flight itself—deliverConfig runs against the local dir with a console recorder, then Flight 1 boots, writes the delivered config, and runs checks against it directly.

Final decision: 2 flights per lane. F0 is a baseline boot establishing health evidence for the delivery transaction, and F1 boots with the old defaults, spawns, writes the orchestrator-delivered file, runs the reload command, and verifies new values plus a bad-value rejection case (saveConfigValues with health 5000 should get a 422).

Also checking previewConfig errors and deliverConfig refusal on preflight for that same bad value, plus a hand-written bad value on the server that should get clamped at reload time. Now I need to write the script, verifying the testflight paths and classpath files on node-2 exist via a devhost run first.

I'm checking a few potential issues: whether the plugin inventory scan correctly parses plugin.yml from jars rather than just filenames, and whether the health check's regex for detecting "FrostMobs: enabled" matches what the delivery flow actually produces.

I'm also tracing how numeric attribute values like move_speed, max_health, and attack_damage get rendered into YAML and whether floating-point formatting ("0.3" vs "0.30000001192092896" from the vanilla attribute command) will still match the expected substring in tests, along with whether baseline error comparison during the health check could falsely trigger a rollback due to sandbox log noise.

Checking whether health resets properly after reload (setHealth respecting the newly applied max_health base, including the bad-config case where max health jumps to 1024), confirming the reload command string gets stripped of its slash correctly, and verifying that default attribute values like armor and attack_knockback for zombies match what the orchestrator expects after applying CyrusSettings defaults.

Also confirming API compatibility: Attribute constants work fine as interface statics in this Paper version with only deprecation warnings (not errors), and that setPersistent/setRemoveWhenFarAway are valid Entity/LivingEntity methods for marking mobs persistent.

There's a potential ambiguity risk with the two-argument spawn method lacking a consumer versus the consumer-overload, since both an old org.bukkit.util.Consumer and the newer java.util.function.Consumer variant might coexist and cause a lambda overload conflict. Safer to avoid that entirely by spawning without a consumer and configuring the entity afterward with a separate call.

Checking that "difficulty easy" isn't a reserved keyword, flat-world zombie spawn with AI disabled at the world spawn point, and that the nearest-sort selector resolves correctly from console position — also confirming the attribute checks still apply correctly when only one zombie exists before a second spawns in.

I'm puzzled why the spawned zombie count comes back as zero after the RCON spawn command—maybe the world has spawn-monsters disabled or a gamerule like doMobSpawning is blocking it, even though difficulty was set to easy beforehand.

Actually it's more likely a chunk-loading issue: if Test Flight sets spawnChunkRadius to 0 to save memory, the entity could be spawning into an unloaded chunk, so querying for entities finds nothing. I'm planning to force-load or add a plugin chunk ticket to the target chunk before spawning to make sure it stays loaded and trackable.

For the health check failure, I realize "answered" shouldn't depend on whether flight A passed — it should be computed from whether the rcon plugins check returned valid evidence. I'm fixing that so a passing plugins check properly marks the server as answered, then rerunning both fixes.

push_files() {
  # Source only: git-tracked + untracked-not-ignored files. node_modules, .next,
  # .git and every .env* stay where they are (rsync never deletes excluded files).
  # shellcheck disable=SC2086

    --exclude='/.env' --exclude='/.env.*' --include='.env.example' --exclude='.env*' \
    --exclude=/.devhost-owner --exclude=/.devhost-deps --exclude='/tsconfig.tsbuildinfo' \
    --filter=':- .gitignore' \
    "$TOP/" "$BUILD_HOST:$WS/"
}

## Cyrus Config and Stats Studio (2026-10-10, branch `feature/cyrus-r23-config`, NOT deployed, flag OFF)

Manual editors for every number a mod can tune (mob health/speed/damage, weapon fire rate/reload/ammo/spread, ability cooldowns, shop prices, boss phases, quest rewards, arena timers...), so nobody has to prompt the AI to change a value. Plan: `docs/cyrus/config/CONFIG-PLAN.md` (copy in `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-designs/v5-config/`). Code: `lib/cyrus/config/` (pure core is client-safe), host seam respected (no new Nxeon imports under `lib/cyrus`).

**Model (ONE param model).** `ConfigSpec` v1 (`spec.ts`, JSON Schema `config.v1.schema.json`): groups; params of type number / int / duration (`durationUnit` ticks|s|ms) / range / bool / enum / text / color / sound-ref / asset-ref / list / table; `min`/`max` = HARD limits (refused by the editor, clamped by the generated loader), `safe` = balanced range (warning only), unit, step, label + help, `applies` = live | reload | restart (reload needs `reload.command`), `visual` = viewport link (clipRate / attackRate / scale / fireRate / tint), tags, presets. The designers' `Param` maps in through `fromDesignerParams` (designer compile output is byte-identical; its tests unchanged). ModSpec v1 has an optional `config: { spec, values? }` section (validated with the ConfigSpec rules; `modspec.v1.schema.json` regenerated).

**Core.** `values.ts` (coercion, strict/clamp checks, balance warnings, seconds display), `diff.ts` (diff/patch with stale-`from` conflicts, invert = undo, reset, presets, `appliesFor`), `yamldoc.ts` + `file.ts` (comment-preserving config.yml editor: only changed value spans move; comments, quoting, unknown keys, CRLF kept; block scalars / anchors / multi-line flow refused; `renderConfigYml` writes a commented file from a spec), `infer.ts` (schema inference from an existing config.yml: types, ranges/enums/units from comments, durations from key suffixes, tables from lists of maps, reload command from plugin.yml), `templates.ts` (12 category templates: mob, melee, gun, armor, ability, boss, shop, quest, minigame, world, item, utility, with easy/normal/hard presets; `suggestTemplates` zero-token routing), `visual.ts` (`visualEffects` + `applyToClock(any {setSpeed})`: Model Studio `PlaybackClock` today, Motion core clock later), `verify.ts` (build check: every declared key read; undeclared reads and hard-coded stat numbers are warnings), `exporters.ts` (per-game exporter contract; Paper YAML exporter verified; FiveM/Hytale planned; `javaSettingsClass` = typed Java class that reads + clamps every key), `edit.ts` (`planConfigEdit`, the deterministic "set X to N" recogniser).

**Build.** With `CYRUS_CONFIG_STUDIO=1` the portal route (`route.ts`, called from `lib/cyrus/assets/request.ts`) gives plain plugin builds (never designer builds) `assets.config` + up to 3 template ids. The service adds the SETTINGS prompt section and the template keys (user turn), and `services/modbuilder/configs.js` (validator bundled from lib/cyrus/config as `config-spec.js`, regenerate with `npx tsx scripts/cyrus/build-config-artifacts.ts`) checks `assets/config/schema.json`: schema rules -> unread keys (one repair, then dropped) -> a reload command missing from plugin.yml turns reload into restart -> config.yml written FROM the schema (existing file keeps comments and extra keys) -> `assetResult.config`. The portal re-validates it (`sync.ts`) and stores `ModBuild.result.cyrusConfig`. Off: request, prompts and results are byte-identical.

**Values-only edits.** `service.ts` + `http.ts` + `/api/cyrus/config/v1` (GET view; POST preview | save | revert | plan | deliver). Schema source order: declared -> designer (designs compiled again) -> inferred from the jar's config.yml. A save = `CyrusRevision` kind `config` (manifest with the new config.yml sha) + `CyrusProjectAsset` kind `config` key `values` (values, patch, config.yml text); `expectedHeadId` -> 409 on a stale editor. No model, no build, no tokens. No DB migration (kind columns are strings). Delivery: `deliverConfig` in `lib/cyrus/delivery/orchestrator.ts` (same journal/rollback transaction; merges the values into the server's CURRENT file; reload = the mod's own command over the console, a failing reply rolls back and reloads the old file; restart settings restart + health). Needs `CYRUS_DELIVERY=1` AND `CYRUS_CONFIG_STUDIO=1`; the API's `deliver` answers 501 until the worker has an enqueue path.

**UI.** `/dashboard/cyrus/<buildId>/studio/config` (`components/cyrus/studios/ConfigStudio.tsx`, `config-studio.css`), Config link in the studio switch: groups rail, search, presets, slider + typed field with unit and the balanced band, per-setting reset, balance warnings, applies badges, review drawer with the exact config.yml lines, Save revision, History + Undo, the "type it" box (no AI), and a preview stage on `PlaybackClock` (walk/attack/fire/reload clip speed and size follow the stats). Dark + light; phones are read only. Mockups `v5-config/config-mob.html`, `config-gun.html`; screenshots `impl-shots/config-*.png`. Not plan-gated (owner decision pending).

**Verified.** Unit: `test/cyrus-config.test.ts`, `test/cyrus-config-integration.test.ts`. Real node-2 Test Flight on Paper 1.21.11 (JDK 21) and 26.2 (JDK 25): `test/cyrus-config-real.ts` -> `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-research/config-flights-2026-10-10.json` (mob stats via the generated settings class, studio save, deliverConfig, live `/frostmobs reload`, new values confirmed by vanilla `attribute ... base get`, 5000 hp refused by the studio and clamped to 1024 on the server, a bad speed falls back to its default). Not verified: a real client, a real AI build declaring a schema (no paid model calls), delivery through the worker, FiveM/Hytale exporters.
EOF

## Config and Stats Studio (`feature/cyrus-r23-config`, worktree cyrus-r23, 2026-10-10) - NOT deployed, flag OFF
New OFF flag `CYRUS_CONFIG_STUDIO` (env; route + page + API + deliverConfig). No migration, no enum, no table (revision kind `config` and asset kind `config` are strings). Docs: "Cyrus Config and Stats Studio". Report: `U-config-studio.md`. Decide:
1. **Plan gate:** proposed UNGATED on every plan (editing numbers is not asset creation; ownership/auth checked server side, fail closed).
2. **Billing:** values-only saves and deliveries call no model and cost 0 tokens. Confirm they stay free.
3. **"Just tweak a setting" recogniser** (`planConfigEdit`): wired only into the studio's "type it" box (no AI). Wiring it into the normal change-request path skips the model (changes billing, same open question as the designers' `planDesignEdit`). Approve or keep studio-only?
4. **Delivery:** `deliverConfig` exists (journal + rollback + reload/restart) but nothing enqueues it; the API answers 501 for "send to server" until the worker path for `CYRUS_DELIVERY` exists. Reload automatically after a save, or a "Deliver" click per change?
5. **Balance warnings** (template `safe` ranges are design judgement, not measurement): show to customers, or owner/admin first?
6. **Switch order:** `CYRUS_CONFIG_STUDIO=1` on the web + build-service request side after the image rebuild; delivery after `CYRUS_DELIVERY`.
7. Phones are read only by design (confirm).
EOF

# U: Cyrus Config and Stats Studio (2026-10-10)

Branch `feature/cyrus-r23-config` (worktree `/tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-r23`), built on `feature/cyrus-r2` and merged with the latest r2 before finishing. NOT deployed, flag `CYRUS_CONFIG_STUDIO` OFF, no migration.

## What was built (each step its own commit)
1. **Plan**: `docs/cyrus/config/CONFIG-PLAN.md` (copy in `cyrus-designs/v5-config/`): ConfigSpec v1, ModSpec relation, 12 category templates, AI declaration + build verification, values-only storage, delivery, inference, presets/diff/undo, exporter contract, risks, owner decisions.
2. **Pure core** `lib/cyrus/config/`: Zod + JSON Schema ConfigSpec (12 param types, hard limits vs balanced range, units, `applies` live/reload/restart, `visual` viewport links, presets); 12 templates as data (mob, melee, gun, armor, ability, boss, shop, quest, minigame, world, item, utility); value checks (strict/clamp, balance warnings); diff/patch/invert/reset/presets; comment-preserving config.yml editor (byte-identical round trip, CRLF, quoting, unknown keys); schema inference from config.yml + plugin.yml; designer `Param` -> ConfigSpec mapping (one param model; designer output unchanged); `visualEffects` + `applyToClock` for any `setSpeed` clock.
3. **Integration**: ModSpec optional `config` section; revision kind `config`, asset kind `config`; portal route (plain plugin builds only) -> service SETTINGS prompt part + template keys; `services/modbuilder/configs.js` (bundled validator `config-spec.js`): schema rules, unread keys repaired then dropped, missing reload command -> restart, config.yml written from the schema; portal re-validation into `ModBuild.result.cyrusConfig`; values-only service + `/api/cyrus/config/v1` (view, preview, save, revert, plan, deliver); `deliverConfig` in the delivery orchestrator (journal, merge into the server's current file, mod reload command or restart, rollback on a failing reply); `planConfigEdit` ("set X to N", no AI) wired only to the studio's type-it box; Paper `javaSettingsClass` (reads + clamps every key).
4. **Real flights** (`test/cyrus-config-real.ts`, results `config-flights-2026-10-10.json`).
5. **Studio UI**: 2 mockups (`v5-config/config-mob.html`, `config-gun.html`, shots in `v5-config/shots/`), then `/dashboard/cyrus/<id>/studio/config` (`ConfigStudio.tsx`): groups, search, presets, sliders with the balanced band + unit fields, reset, warnings, applies badges, review drawer with the exact config.yml lines, Save revision, History/Undo, type-it box, preview stage on Model Studio's `PlaybackClock`; dark, light, phone read only. Screenshots `impl-shots/config-*.png`.
6. Docs section "Cyrus Config and Stats Studio", OWNER-ACTIONS section, this report.

## RAN
- Unit: `test/cyrus-config-studio.test.ts` (29) + `test/cyrus-config-integration.test.ts` (19): schema rules, all templates validate with zero warnings, values, diff/undo, YAML round trips on 6 realistic fixtures, inference on 6 fixtures + the designer config.yml, designer mapping reads the designer file exactly, verify, service bundle current, service round (repair/drop/infer), prompt byte-identity when off, portal route, ModSpec section, recogniser, values service + HTTP (404 gates, 409 stale head, undo), deliverConfig against a fake server (reload, failed reload rolls back byte-identical and reloads again, restart, refusals).
- Full suite after the r2 merge + `devhost tsc`: numbers in the docs/handoff (see final report).
- **Real node-2 Test Flight, Paper 1.21.11 (JDK 21) and 26.2 (JDK 25), both PASSED**: mob template schema -> config.yml + generated settings class; `verifyTunables` 7/7 read; javac 0 warnings; flight A: frost zombie spawned with default stats (20 hp, 0.23, 3 dmg, 1.0 scale) confirmed by the plugin and vanilla `attribute ... base get`; studio save (revision kind config) refused 5000 hp (`invalid_values`); `deliverConfig` (real orchestrator, journaled copy of the server dir) merged the values and issued `frostmobs reload`; flight B: delivered file written + that command on the live server -> existing and new zombies at 60 hp / 0.3 / 7 dmg / 1.5 scale (vanilla reads: "The base value of attribute Max Health for entity Zombie is 60.0", Speed 0.3, Scale 1.5, Attack Damage 7.0); a hand-edited bad file (5000 hp, "fast") -> "clamped ... 5000.0 -> 1024.0" and "move_speed is not a number; using 0.23". No leftover flight dirs.
- devhost dev server + Playwright: 7 screenshots including a real save through the API ("Saved as revision 1. Takes effect with /arsenal reload.").

## NOT run / not verified
- No real AI build declaring a schema (no paid model calls); the SETTINGS prompt is untested against a model.
- The orchestrator's console during the flight was a recorder (the issued command was replayed by Test Flight on the live server); no persistent live server session and no worker enqueue path, so the API's "send to server" answers 501.
- No real Minecraft client; no in-game behaviour beyond attributes read from the console.
- Designer mods: schema derived and read/write tested in unit tests only (no flight of a studio edit on a designer jar; the designer's own flights cover its reload).
- FiveM / Hytale exporters are contracts only (maturity planned).
- Motion core clock: `applyToClock` is structural (`setSpeed`); tested with `PlaybackClock` only.

## Notes
- `lib/cyrus/config.ts` (host paths, merged from r2) shares the name with the `lib/cyrus/config/` directory: bare `lib/cyrus/config` resolves to the file; import the studio core as `lib/cyrus/config/index` or per file. My unit test was renamed to `test/cyrus-config-studio.test.ts` (r2 owns `test/cyrus-config.test.ts`).
- Owner decisions: OWNER-ACTIONS "Config and Stats Studio".

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

input.message:
All six deliverables are finished on `feature/cyrus-r23-config` (worktree `/tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-r23`, HEAD bdef3c5ba4), each committed separately. The latest `feature/cyrus-r2` was merged twice. Nothing deployed; new flag `CYRUS_CONFIG_STUDIO` is off; no migration.

1. **Plan**: `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-designs/v5-config/CONFIG-PLAN.md` (~1,880 words, slightly over target; copy in `docs/cyrus/config/`).
2. **Pure core** in `lib/cyrus/config/`: ConfigSpec v1, 12 category templates, value checks, diff/undo, comment-preserving config.yml read/write, inference from existing config.yml, designer params mapped in (designer output unchanged).
3. **Integration**: optional ModSpec `config` section; build declares and checks settings, config.yml written from the schema; values-only revisions and API; `deliverConfig` in the orchestrator; "type it" box (studio only).
4. **Real node-2 flights passed on Paper 1.21.11 and 26.2**: vanilla `attribute` reads confirmed the new stats after a live reload. The studio refused 5000 hp; a hand-edited 5000 hp was clamped to 1024 on the server.
5. **UI**: 2 mockups, Config page, 7 screenshots in `impl-shots/config-*.png` (dark, light, phone read-only), one with a real save.
6. Docs section, OWNER-ACTIONS section, report `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-research/U-config-studio.md`.

**Tests**: full suite 2157/2160; the 3 failures were the r2 API OpenAPI contract, regenerated (rerun 154/154). tsc clean.

**Not done**: no real AI build, no worker path for "send to server" (API returns 501), no real client.

**Owner decisions**: ungated plan, free saves, recogniser wiring, auto-reload, balance warnings.
